cookingSessions.label: Big cook session
cookingSessions.kitchenNote: Do this early morning before shared kitchen gets busy. Use multiple burners simultaneously: rice on one, daal on another, meat on third.

cookItems.name: Chicken karahi base
cookItems.instructions: Cook chicken in thick tomato-onion masala (ginger-garlic, haldi, zeera, lal mirch). Use 1 tbsp oil only. Cook until oil separates and masala is thick. Do NOT add water — dry-style stores better.
cookItems.storageNote: Store in airtight containers. Label with date.

usedInMeals.use: Reheat 1 portion with saag and roti
Mix with batch rice for quick biryani-style

cookItems.name: Haleem (batch)
cookItems.instructions: Combine wheat (soaked overnight), masoor + moong lentils, and chicken in pressure cooker. Cook 45 min. Blend partially with hand blender. Add zeera-onion tarka. Season with kala namak and lemon.
cookItems.storageNote: Refrigerate 3 portions. Freeze 2 as emergency backup. Haleem freezes extremely well — no quality loss.

usedInMeals.use: Reheat 1 portion (3 min microwave) + boiled egg

cookItems.name: Hard-boiled eggs
cookItems.instructions: Place eggs in cold water. Bring to boil. Cook 10 min. Transfer to ice water 5 min. Store IN SHELL — do not peel until ready to eat. Peeled eggs deteriorate fast.
cookItems.storageNote: Store in original egg carton or bowl in fridge. Do not peel until eating.

cookItems.name: Brown rice (large batch)
cookItems.instructions: Rinse rice 3 times. Cook 1:2 ratio (600g rice : 1200ml water). Bring to boil, reduce to lowest heat, cover tightly 35 min. Fluff with fork. Cool completely before portioning — hot rice stored airtight causes sogginess.
cookItems.storageNote: Cool fully before sealing. Reheat with 1 tbsp water in microwave 2 min, covered.

cookItems.name: Saag (mustard greens)
cookItems.instructions: Wash and roughly chop greens. Cook in pressure cooker 15 min OR stovetop 25 min until fully soft. Blend lightly — keep some texture. Add ginger-garlic, haldi. Store plain — add fresh tarka (zeera + garlic) each time you reheat to refresh flavour.
cookItems.storageNote: Saag intensifies in flavour as it sits — actually tastes better on day 2 and 3.

usedInMeals.use: Served with chicken karahi and roti

cookItems.name: Daal mash (urad daal)
cookItems.instructions: Wash daal. Pressure cook with haldi and salt 20 min. Mash partially. Prepare tarka: heat 1 tsp oil, add zeera, garlic slices, dried red chilli — pour over daal. Cool before storing. Add FRESH tarka each time you reheat a portion to keep it tasting just-cooked.
cookItems.storageNote: Daal thickens in fridge. Add 2–3 tbsp water when reheating and stir.

usedInMeals.use: Daal tadka with saag and roti

cookItems.name: Whole wheat rotis
cookItems.instructions: Make dough: 400g whole wheat flour + water + pinch salt. Rest 20 min. Roll thin. Cook on hot dry tawa 45 sec each side. Stack immediately and wrap tightly in a clean cloth while hot — this steams them soft. Once cool, transfer to foil-wrapped bundles of 2.
cookItems.storageNote: Reheat on dry tawa 30–45 sec per side. Or microwave 30 sec wrapped in damp paper towel.

prepAhead: Soak wheat overnight (Saturday night) for haleem
Soak urad daal 2 hours before cooking
Wash and rough-chop saag before starting cook session

cookingSessions.label: Mid-week top-up
cookingSessions.kitchenNote: Quick session. Fish must be cooked fresh — never store more than 2 days. Koftas bake passively while you prep other things.

cookItems.name: Salmon / fish curry
cookItems.instructions: Cook fish in light tomato-onion masala. Add fish last — cook only 8–10 min on medium heat until just cooked through. Do not overcook. Serve same day or next day only.
cookItems.storageNote: Fish MUST be consumed within 2 days. Never freeze cooked fish curry.

usedInMeals.use: Fresh portion with roti and raita

cookItems.name: Baked koftas
cookItems.instructions: Mix mince with 1 egg, chopped onion, zeera, coriander, green chilli. Shape into 8 balls. Place on lined baking tray. Bake 200°C 20 min while you cook other things. Cool then refrigerate. Cook kofta masala sauce separately (10 min) — store sauce and koftas together.
cookItems.storageNote: Koftas stay moist in sauce. Reheat in pan with lid, 5 min on low.

cookItems.name: Boiled chickpeas
cookItems.instructions: Soak chickpeas from Tuesday night. Pressure cook Wednesday with salt and haldi 20 min. Do NOT season yet — store plain boiled. Season each portion fresh (lemon + zeera + chaat masala + coriander) when eating. Plain boiled lasts longer.
cookItems.storageNote: Store in cooking water — keeps them moist. Drain when using.

cookItems.name: Fresh rotis (second batch)
cookItems.instructions: Same method as Sunday batch. Cook 6 rotis for Thu–Sun. Wrap in foil pairs.
cookItems.storageNote: Reheat on tawa 30–45 sec per side.

prepAhead: Soak chickpeas Tuesday night
Defrost fish in fridge from Tuesday night if using frozen

cookingSessions.label: Big cook session
cookingSessions.kitchenNote: Week 2 introduces aloo gosht and keema. Both cook well together on adjacent burners. Start rice cooker first as it takes longest.

cookItems.name: Aloo gosht (lamb + potato)
cookItems.instructions: Brown lamb in 1 tbsp oil. Add onion-tomato masala (ginger-garlic, zeera, haldi, lal mirch). Pressure cook 20 min. Add peeled cubed potato, pressure cook 10 more min. Oil should separate on top — skim if excessive. Cool before portioning.
cookItems.storageNote: Potato absorbs masala overnight — tastes better day 2+. Reheat in pan with 2 tbsp water.

cookItems.name: Beef keema with peas
cookItems.instructions: Cook mince in onion-tomato masala with ginger-garlic, zeera, garam masala. Break up lumps as it cooks. Add peas last 5 min. Cook until liquid fully evaporates — dry keema stores much better than wet. Add fresh coriander after cooling.
cookItems.storageNote: Freeze 1–2 portions. Thaw overnight in fridge. Reheat with splash of water in pan.

cookItems.name: Hard-boiled eggs
cookItems.instructions: Same as Week 1. Cold water start, boil 10 min, ice bath, store in shell.
cookItems.storageNote: In-shell only. Do not peel ahead.

cookItems.name: Brown rice (large batch)
cookItems.instructions: Identical to Week 1. 1:2 ratio. Cool fully before portioning into 7 containers.
cookItems.storageNote: Reheat with 1 tbsp water, microwave 2 min covered.

cookItems.name: Spinach daal (masoor + palak)
cookItems.instructions: Cook masoor daal with haldi and salt 20 min until soft. Add roughly chopped spinach, cook 10 more min. Blend lightly — keep texture. Prepare garlic tarka separately and add half now, save half to add when reheating each portion.
cookItems.storageNote: Add fresh garlic tarka when reheating each portion — makes it taste freshly made.

usedInMeals.use: With roti as kali daal alternative

cookItems.name: Murgh shorba (chicken broth)
cookItems.instructions: Simmer chicken with whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf), ginger, haldi in 1.5L water 45 min. Remove bones, shred chicken back into broth. Add light tomato-ginger seasoning. Divide into 2 portions.
cookItems.storageNote: Fat will solidify on top when cold — skim or stir in. Both are fine.

usedInMeals.use: Full portion as murgh shorba with rice

cookItems.name: Whole wheat rotis

Defrost lamb from freezer Saturday if using frozen

cookItems.name: Baked shami kebabs
cookItems.instructions: Cook chana daal until soft, drain. Mix with mince, 1 egg, zeera, coriander, green chilli, ginger-garlic. Blend coarsely — keep some texture. Shape into 8 patties. Bake 190°C 22 min flipping halfway. Refrigerate when cool.
cookItems.storageNote: Reheat in oven 180°C 10 min or pan on low with lid. Add raita fresh when serving.

cookItems.name: Mutton yakhni pulao
cookItems.instructions: Cook mutton with whole spices in 600ml water 25 min. Remove mutton, strain broth. Cook rice in strained broth 15 min. Combine. This gives biryani-level flavour with minimal effort. Store as 2 full portions.
cookItems.storageNote: Pulao dries slightly in fridge. Add 2 tbsp water when reheating, cover tightly.

cookItems.name: Saag gosht (lamb + greens)
cookItems.instructions: Use any leftover lamb from aloo gosht or fresh small piece. Cook with mustard greens and spinach until completely soft. Add garlic-ginger paste, haldi. Blend lightly. High iron and Vit A — one of the most nutrient-dense dishes in the plan.
cookItems.storageNote: Tastes better day 2. Add tiny knob of ghee when reheating.

cookItems.name: Chicken palak (spinach-chicken gravy)
cookItems.instructions: Blanch spinach 3 min, blend smooth. In same pan, cook chicken with onion-garlic-ginger, haldi, zeera until cooked through. Add blended spinach. Simmer 10 min. This base works as palak chicken, can be served dry as karahi-style, or thinned as shorba.
cookItems.storageNote: Versatile base — can serve thick (palak chicken) or thin it with water (shorba). Iron + protein combo.

usedInMeals.use: Served drier as karahi style with rice
Biryani base — mix with batch rice

cookItems.name: Baked egg muffins (vegetable)
cookItems.instructions: Whisk 12 eggs. Finely chop: 1 capsicum, 1 onion, handful spinach, 2 green chillies. Mix veg into eggs with salt, haldi, zeera. Pour into greased muffin tray (12 cups). Bake 180°C 18 min until set and lightly golden. Cool fully before refrigerating in batches of 3.
cookItems.storageNote: Reheat 90 sec in microwave or 5 min in 160°C oven. Do not overheat — rubbery texture. Best eaten slightly warm.

cookItems.name: Beef keema (batch)
cookItems.instructions: Cook lean mince dry-style with onion, tomato, ginger-garlic, zeera, garam masala. Dry keema is key — cook until no liquid remains. Cool fully. This batch serves double duty: keema matar dinner AND stuffed karela filling.
cookItems.storageNote: Freeze 1 portion. Dry keema freezes perfectly.

usedInMeals.use: Keema matar — add frozen peas while reheating

cookItems.instructions: Cook masoor daal and mustard greens together in one pot — saves washing up. Add haldi, ginger-garlic, salt. Blend lightly. Serve as both daal and saag together. Versatile — reheats as daal one day, as saag another depending on consistency.
cookItems.storageNote: Add fresh garlic tarka when reheating. Add water to thin if needed.

usedInMeals.use: Moong daal style with rice and raita

cookItems.instructions: Soak rajma Saturday night. Pressure cook 25 min until completely soft. Prepare onion-tomato masala separately, add rajma and mash a few beans to thicken. Season with amchur, zeera, kala namak. Portion into 4 containers.
cookItems.storageNote: Rajma freezes perfectly. Freeze 1 portion for emergencies.

cookItems.name: Haleem (extra-large batch)
cookItems.instructions: Cook largest batch yet. Pressure cook soaked wheat + lentils + chicken 60 min. Blend partially. Tarka: caramelised onion + zeera + ginger julienne. Portion into 5. Freeze 2 for future weeks.

cookItems.name: Chicken saag + karahi dual batch
cookItems.instructions: Split 700g chicken into two pans. Pan 1 (350g): cook in spinach gravy — chicken saag style. Pan 2 (350g): cook dry-style karahi with fresh tomatoes, capsicum, ginger. Both take 25–30 min. Gives two distinct flavour profiles from one cook session.
cookItems.storageNote: Keep saag and karahi in separate containers — different uses across the week.

cookItems.name: Daal makhani (overnight slow-cook)
cookItems.cookMethod: Start Saturday night on lowest heat — 8+ hrs (OR pressure cook 45 min)
cookItems.instructions: Saturday night: wash lentils, soak 2 hrs, pressure cook 45 min. Transfer to pot, add onion-tomato masala, 1 tbsp cream, simmer overnight on absolute lowest heat. Sunday morning: stir, season, portion. The overnight method creates restaurant-depth flavour.
cookItems.storageNote: Thickens significantly in fridge. Add 3–4 tbsp water and stir when reheating.
